title: Mortgage Rates Surge, Foreclosures Reach 2008 Levels, What's Next? | Ron Butler
speaker: Ron Butler

macro_themes.view: Fixed-income executives he talks to have highest conviction that bond yields of all types, especially long-term, will be higher next year, with dips along the way.
He would take the higher contract on 30-year mortgage rates going above 7.5%; higher for longer is the big issue.
Central banks will keep raising; Bank of Canada hikes either October 28 or December despite weak jobs.
Prices keep falling through half or all of 2027 as foreclosures and below-comp court-ordered sales reset values; no real recovery until 2028, tiny condos worst.
High rates and buyer reticence mean new-home construction and builders will get worse.

calls.instrument_quoted: Government bond yields / US 30-year mortgage rate (~7.4-7.5%)
calls.reason: Synchronized global setup of central banks hiking and bearish bond sentiment among fixed-income bosses; trend over 3-6 months is higher yields and mortgage rates despite short-term dips.
calls.quote: their belief is their highest conviction is the trend next year will be higher.

calls.reason: Builders can't incentivize past high mortgage rates and buyers are waiting, so completions and homebuilders keep weakening.
calls.quote: They're absolutely correlated and they're going to get worse.

notes: Date not stated in transcript (refers to US CPI 'this week' and Canada CPI next Monday); listing date used. Bond-yield call is generic 'all yields higher next year'; mapped to TNX since the host says 30y mortgages track the 10-year. XHB 'getting worse' refers to construction/builders broadly, price 95 quoted by host. Housing price views (Canada) are not tradable tickers and are in macro_themes only.
